comment: Round 22 — AnchorerWorker production signing path (Ed25519MoveSigner) per soland/src/routing/anchor_admin.rs::service_admin_signer + arkret-rust-sdk/crates/signatures/src/signer.rs. Validates the deterministic-vs-ephemeral seed contract: (a) configured-seed signer is byte-deterministic (same seed + same canonical body ⇒ same JWS signature segment) so anchor signatures replay across restart; (b) ephemeral-seed signer is non-deterministic across runs because the seed is fresh randomness; (c) different seeds produce different signatures even for the same canonical body (key-binding); (d) signature verifies via verify_ed25519_move_signature using the signer's derived verifying key (round-trip closure). Each vector pins a normative input (seed source + canonical-body hash) and the outcome shape; no real ed25519 ops run here — covered by SDK signature crate unit tests. The validator is structural.

expected.rationale: Configured 32-byte seed + same canonical body bytes ⇒ identical Ed25519 signature on every invocation. JWS payload-hash and signature segment are byte-stable. AnchorerWorker uses this path for restart-replay safety.

soland's service_admin_signer derives seed = sha256('soland:service-signer:' + service_id). Pure function of service_id ⇒ same admin Move signature every boot for the same service identity (dev-mode replay safety; production swaps for HSM).

Ephemeral seed = fresh CSPRNG bytes per signer construction ⇒ different signing key each run. Even with identical canonical body the JWS signature segment differs across processes. Used for one-shot test fixtures and ephemeral peer scenarios; MUST NOT be used for AnchorerWorker production path (would break restart-replay).

Key-binding: signature s = sign(sk, m). Same m, distinct sk ⇒ distinct s. Confirms Ed25519MoveSigner is not silently reusing a global key; each MoveSigner instance carries its own SigningKey from its own seed.

Round-trip: signer.sign_payload(m) ⇒ MoveSignature; verify_ed25519_move_signature(m, sig, signer.verifying_key()) returns Ok(()). The verifying key is derived from the same SigningKey ⇒ closes the loop without DID-resolver dependency.

MoveSignature.payload_digest = sha256:<hex of canonical body>. The receiver re-derives the canonical body bytes and recomputes sha256; must equal the declared payload_digest before verifying the JWS sig segment. Wire-form invariant for detached JWS (RFC 7515 §3.2).
Verifying with a key derived from a different seed ⇒ signature does not validate. Ed25519 has no malleability; verifier MUST reject.

After signing, an attacker mutates the canonical body bytes. payload_digest declared in MoveSignature no longer matches sha256(tampered_body). verify_ed25519_move_signature MUST reject before invoking the JWS-segment ed25519 verify.
